stage: S1 shared metadata and interleaved construction
identity_configuration: one ordinary user, one client; all test resources owned by that user

fixtures.input: two distinct synthetic PDFs; no personal content
fixtures.identity_binding: returned task identifier -> successful ingestion -> documented related document identifier; never infer from max id or title alone

preconditions: ordinary user permissions explicitly granted and recorded
upload/task polling transport qualified against local contract
each ingestion completes within bounded timeout
all HTTP emitted through interfaces; stories choose the action order

steps: create tag T and document type Y
attach T and Y to A
attach T and Y to B
read A, B, T and Y
oracles: stable A/B ids and distinct file checksums
exact expected tag ids and document_type ids on each read
metadata names and links agree with latest accepted writes

cases.intent: Modify shared metadata between relationship construction steps
steps: create T and Y; ingest A and B
attach T and Y to A; read both documents
rename T; read T, A and B
attach T and Y to B; read both documents
rename Y; read Y, A and B
oracles: both documents reference original metadata ids
unrelated document fields and file checksums remain unchanged
display fields checked only where specified by the response schema

cases.intent: Local link removal does not affect another document
steps: create T and Y; ingest A and B; attach both to both documents
detach T from A; read A and B
change B title; read A and B
reattach T to A; read A and B
oracles: A tag set changes exactly as requested
B title change leaves A unchanged

evidence: response status and full JSON bodies after each write/read
next_identity_configurations: same ordinary user with two client contexts and separate runtime bindings
two ordinary users with explicitly authorized shared resources
two ordinary users with private resources: defer authorization regression implementation to a separately scoped fixture/policy review
next_mechanisms: copy isolation where supported by contract
shared metadata lifecycle on owned fixtures
reset/replay on an isolated disposable environment
classification: same invariant and mechanism across orders = one candidate defect with multiple reproductions; do not count each HTTP 500 as a new bug
